'''Lonnie Walker IV''' (born December 14, 1998) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Miami Hurricanes men's basketball|Miami Hurricanes]]. He played [[high school]] basketball for [[Reading Senior High School (Reading, Pennsylvania)|Reading High School]] in Pennsylvania. He signed a letter of intent to continue his academic and athletic career at the [[University of Miami]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/18062752/five-star-recruit-lonnie-walker-commits-miami-hurricanes | title = Five Star Recruit Lonnie Walker commits to Miami Hurricanes | work = espn | date = 17 November 2016 | accessdate = 20 February 2017}}</ref> In January 2017 Walker was selected as an [[2017 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|McDonald's All-American]].<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.maxpreps.com/news/-c4H_udHpk68Wy2LGvrS3Q/2017-mcdonald’s-all-american-game-boys-rosters-announced.htm | title = 2017 McDonald’s All-American Game boys rosters announced | work = maxpreps | date = 15 January 2017 | accessdate = 20 February 2017}}</ref> On March 25, 2017, Walker led the Red Knights to their first state championship in the program's 117 year history in a 64-60 win over the [[Pine-Richland High School|Pine-Richland Rams]]. Walker finished the game with 22 points, 8 rebounds, 4 steals, and 3 assists.<ref>http://rawsports.tv/wp/reading-high-are-the-state-champs-for-the-first-time-ever-by-trey-erdman/</ref>

==Early years==
Walker attended [[Reading Senior High School (Reading, Pennsylvania)|Reading High School]] in [[Reading, Pennsylvania]]. Walker made his varsity basketball debut as a freshman and played 27 games averaging 8 points per game, and later as a sophomore he averaged 16.9 points per game in a short season due to injury. And in 29 games, as a junior, he averaged 17.1 points per game. During his senior year he averaged a career best 18.4 points per game and surpassed Reading High grad and former NBA player Donyell Marshall's school record in points by finishing with 1,828. He would lead Reading to their first Pennsylvania State Championship. During the season Walker signed with the [[Miami Hurricanes]], passing on offers from [[Villanova Wildcats men's basketball|Villanova]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], [[Syracuse University|Syracuse]] and [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]].<ref>{{cite web | URL = http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/207877/lonnie-walker | title = Lonnie Walker recruiting profile | work = espn | accessdate = 20 February 2017}}</ref>

==College career==
Walker made his collegiate debut on November 10, 2017, recording 10 points and a season-high 5 assists coming off the bench in a 77–45 blowout win over [[Gardner-Webb University]]. He created new highs of 12 points and 5 rebounds on December 2 in an 80–52 blowout win against [[Princeton University]] before recording season-highs of 26 points and 7 rebounds during his first collegiate start three days later in a 69–54 win over [[Boston University]]. Against [[Louisville]], he scored a game-high 25 points including an acrobatic layup in traffic to force overtime. In a game against [[Boston College]], he hit a 3-pointer with two seconds remaining to win 79-78. Walker finished the season averaging 11.5 points per game, leading the Hurricanes.<ref>http://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/acc/university-of-miami/article207974329.html</ref>

After his sole season with Miami concluded, Walker declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]].<ref>http://collegehoopswatch.com/2018/04/07/miami-basketball-lonnie-walker-leaves-for-draft-canes-roster-could-shuffle/</ref>

==Personal life==
During the 2018 [[NBA Draft Combine]], Walker revealed to the public that he believes the world is an illusion.<ref>http://www.miamiherald.com/sports/college/acc/university-of-miami/article211647749.html</ref>
